mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a recession (UNRATE < 2% at trigger).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP recovers within 30 days after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation (CPIAUCSL) falls below 2% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE and a fall in PAYEMS over one month indicates labor market churning with rising unemployment despite stable or growing workforce, signaling economic distress and increased recession risk, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the economy does not enter recession within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production and reduced corporate output, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or INDPRO rebounds above trend within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over two months signals increased housing demand but reduced savings, indicating consumer leverage expansion and potential overextension, which can precede equity market corrections and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and RSAFS decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or consumer credit growth accelerates after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which rapidly raises borrowing costs and depresses risk asset valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps by > 0.75% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the market rallies on the announcement day.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in CPIAUCSL above 4% for four consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, prompting anticipation of sustained monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 3% within two months after trigger.
